---
name: reference-sentry-resolve-in-release-semantics
description: "sentry.obico.io \"resolved in release X\" reopens on events from X itself; use resolve-in-next-release for unreleased fixes, and check the recorded anchor"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: ebd91bcd-6c0f-4a44-8257-cb2f89fc02a4
  modified: 2026-11-24T23:51:59.689Z
---

On sentry.obico.io (self-hosted 23.1.1), an issue resolved with `statusDetails.inRelease = X` REOPENS (set_regression) on the next event whose release is X itself, and on any newer release; only events from older releases stay quiet. Verified 2026-11-02: OBICO-SERVER-B1J and B1C were resolved with `inRelease: "4052"` while 4052 was the live release, and both reopened within 5 hours from 4052 events.

An unreleased fix needs "resolved in next release" (`inNextRelease: true`): events from the release it is anchored to stay quiet, newer releases reopen it (MOONRAKER-OBICO-TT, anchored at moonraker-obico@2.2.3, took 21 events from 2.2.3 without reopening).

**Why:** the API rejects an `inRelease` that does not exist in Sentry yet ("Unable to find a release"), so "resolve in the version that will ship the fix" cannot be set for a future release.

**How to apply:**
- Never use `inRelease` = the currently deployed release for a fix that has not shipped.
- Use `inNextRelease: true`, then read the issue's activity (`set_resolved_in_release` data) and `statusDetails`: the recorded anchor must be the live release. For issues that were merged, or whose latest event is on an older release, the anchor came out stale (4031/4036 instead of 4052) and the issue will reopen on the next event from the live release. Fix those in the Sentry UI or verify after the next event.
- Send the resolve through the project endpoint, `PUT /api/0/projects/sentry/<project-slug>/issues/?id=<id>`. On 2026-11-24 the organization endpoint (`/organizations/sentry/issues/?id=777`, OBICO-MOBILE-21A) anchored to ios@2.32+319, a year-old release; setting it unresolved and resolving again through `/projects/sentry/obico-mobile/issues/` anchored to the live ios@2.42+336.
- After resolving, check later that `set_regression` activity has not appeared.
- When reporting an issue resolved in next release, say it plainly as done: the fix is committed and Sentry now watches the next release for it. "The next release doesn't exist yet" and "users on the current release still hit it" are the expected state, not a caveat. Kenny corrected this framing twice (2026-11-06 and 2026-11-22, JUSPRIN-APP-7).
- Related release-numbering facts: [[project-obico-release-architecture]].

An AI edit after a crash no longer fails to save with "operation version record already exists"

JusPrin wrote a small file under the project's operations/ folder for every
AI edit, named after the edit's action number (t-1.json, t-2.json, ...). The
number comes from a counter in current-state.json, which is written on a
different schedule. Inside a chat turn, edits after the first wrote their
file without saving the counter, so a crash in the next second and a half
left a file ahead of the counter. After a restart the next edit got the same
number, the store refused to overwrite the file, and the person saw a save
failure even though the save itself had happened (Sentry JUSPRIN-APP-K).

Nothing used these files except version cleanup, which kept any version an
operation file named. Undo, "Revert to here", resume and version history all
work from the saved versions themselves. So the files are gone: the store no
longer writes them, cleanup keeps only the current and pinned versions, and
opening a project made by an earlier build deletes its old operations/
folder. Earlier builds recreate the folder when they open a project, so
going back to 2.1.0 or older still works.

After an AI edit outside a chat turn the shell still saves; inside a turn
the turn's end saves once, as before.
EOF

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.
    screenshot.ps1   Screen capture. Must run in-session.
    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.
    winssh.sh        ssh wrapper. winscp.sh: scp wrapper.

## Typical cycle

    ./winscp.sh <local.ps1> guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Invoke-InSession -TaskName "X" ...'
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Take-Screenshot'
    ./winscp.sh guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/shot.png ./shot.png

## Known gap

There is no current JusPrin Windows binary to test. The Build all workflow's
Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with "could not find any
instance of Visual Studio"; last green Windows build was 2026-03-04 and its
artifacts have expired. Either fix that job, or install VS Build Tools on this VM
and build from the cached OrcaSlicer_dep_win64 artifact.

# Building JusPrin from source on the Windows VM

Verified 2026-09-07: full build from a clean VM, then run and screenshotted.
Total ~1h10m of machine time on n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB).

    deps build   22.7 min   (all 24 applicable deps from source)
    slicer build 23.0 min
    output       C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe (261 KB launcher)
                 + OrcaSlicer.dll (122.7 MB — the actual application)

## Order of operations

1. `install-buildtools.ps1` — CMake 4.3.5 (CI pins ~4.3.0), Ninja, Git for
   Windows, Strawberry Perl, and VS 2022 Build Tools with the VCTools workload.
2. Clone the repo (public, no credentials needed). Shallow is fine: the version
   comes from `version.inc`, not git tags.
3. `build-deps-full.ps1` — builds all deps. **Do not use the CI dependency
   artifact**; see below.
4. `build-slicer.ps1` — runs `build_release_vs.bat slicer`.
5. Put Mesa where the app looks for it, then `run-jusprin.cmd`.

## Things that will bite you

**Run long builds as a SCHEDULED TASK, not over SSH.** Windows OpenSSH kills the
whole process tree when the session ends, so a build started from an SSH command
(even detached with Start-Process) dies on disconnect. Register it instead:

    New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "SYSTEM" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest

Two builds racing in one directory corrupt each other — OpenSSL failed with
`C1033: cannot open program database ossl_static.pdb` when that happened here.

**awk must be on PATH.** `deps/PNG/PNG.cmake` passes `-DPNG_PREFIX=prusaslicer_`,
so libpng generates `pngprefix.h` with an awk script. Without awk you get
`AWK-NOTFOUND` in the PNG CMakeCache and then `C1083: Cannot open include file:
'pngprefix.h'`. Git for Windows ships awk — add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin`
to PATH, not just `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd`.

**Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`.** Several bundled CMakeLists still
declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x rejects outright.

**The CI dependency artifact is unusable.** `OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_20260906`
contains a bundle built 2025-10-17, before `deps/Eigen` was added. The source
requires Eigen 5.0.1 and CMake fails at configure with "Could not find a package
configuration file provided by Eigen3". Build deps from source instead.

**Never hard-stop the VM mid-build.** Stopping the instance during the deps build
left 622 of 22,011 installed files as NUL bytes. It surfaced as bogus syntax
errors deep in Boost headers. Detect it with:

    Get-ChildItem $prefix -Recurse -Include *.hpp,*.h,*.cmake |
      # read first 4 KB, flag any file containing byte 0

The fix is a clean rebuild; DL_CACHE keeps all 21 source archives, so it is a
recompile, not a re-download.

**Qhull is expected to be missing.** `deps/CMakeLists.txt` comments it out under
`if (MSVC)` ("Experimental"), so 24 built deps is the complete set on Windows.

## Running it — use the app's own Mesa hook

Do NOT drop opengl32.dll next to the exe. `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` already
handles this: when system OpenGL is below 2.0 it loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll`
itself and prints "MESA OpenGL library was loaded successfully".

    build\src\Release\mesa\opengl32.dll      <- Mesa's, the app loads this
    build\src\Release\libgallium_wgl.dll     <- dependency, resolves from exe dir

Still export `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`: the GCE
virtual display exposes a D3D12 device, and Mesa's d3d12 backend crashes on the
first rendered frame.

## Windows CI is broken for a different reason

`Build all`'s Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is NOT a bug in
`build_release_vs.bat` — the same script picks generator VS 17 2022 here from
`msbuild -version` (17.14.51.32402) and configures fine against a registered
Build Tools instance. The problem is the GitHub runner's environment.
#!/bin/bash
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o IdentitiesOnly=yes \
    -o ConnectTimeout=15 -o LogLevel=ERROR -i ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine \
    guitest@34.135.245.169 "$@"
#!/bin/bash
scp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o IdentitiesOnly=yes \
    -o LogLevel=ERROR -i ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine "$@"
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
function Log($m) { $s = ("[SLICER {0:HH:mm:ss}] {1}" -f (Get-Date), $m); Write-Host $s; Add-Content C:\guitest\slicer-progress.txt $s }

$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine")
$vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
$vsPath = & $vswhere -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath -latest
$env:Path = "$(Join-Path $vsPath 'MSBuild\Current\Bin');$env:Path"
# Several bundled CMakeLists still declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x
# rejects outright unless this compatibility shim is set.
$env:CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM = "3.5"

Set-Content C:\guitest\slicer-progress.txt "slicer build starting $(Get-Date -Format o)"
Log "msbuild: $((& msbuild -version) | Select-Object -Last 1)"
Set-Location C:\src\JusPrin
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
& cmd /c "build_release_vs.bat slicer 2>&1" | Tee-Object -FilePath C:\guitest\slicer-build.log
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$sw.Stop()
Log ("build_release_vs.bat exit=$code elapsed={0:N1} min" -f $sw.Elapsed.TotalMinutes)

Log "--- executables produced ---"
Get-ChildItem "C:\src\JusPrin\build" -Recurse -Filter "*.exe" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 1MB } |
  ForEach-Object { Log ("  {0}  {1:N1} MB" -f $_.FullName, ($_.Length/1MB)) }
exit $code
@echo off
REM Force Mesa's CPU rasterizer: with a D3D12 device present (the GCE virtual
REM display exposes Microsoft Basic Render Driver) Mesa otherwise picks its
REM d3d12 backend, which crashes on the first rendered frame.
set GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe
set LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
cd /d C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release
start "" "C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Small, dependency-free 2026-07-28 MCP client for deliberate local testing.

This is a wire smoke client, not a substitute for the Phase 4 Inspector/production-client
and conformance tests.
"""

import argparse
from contextlib import closing
import http.client
import json
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2026-07-28"


def call(endpoint, method, params=None):
    params = dict(params or {})
    params["_meta"] = {
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": {"name": "jusprin-smoke", "version": "1"},
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": {},
        "progressToken": "smoke-progress",
    }
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream",
        "MCP-Protocol-Version": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        "Mcp-Method": method,
    }
    if "name" in params:
        headers["Mcp-Name"] = params["name"]
    with closing(http.client.HTTPConnection(endpoint.hostname, endpoint.port, timeout=310)) as connection:
        connection.request("POST", endpoint.path, json.dumps({
            "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "smoke", "method": method, "params": params,
        }), headers)
        response = connection.getresponse()
        if response.getheader("Content-Type", "").startswith("text/event-stream"):
            for line in response:
                if line.startswith(b"data: "):
                    message = json.loads(line[6:])
                    if "result" in message or "error" in message:
                        return message
                    print("Progress:", message.get("params", {}).get("message", ""))
            raise RuntimeError("MCP stream closed without a terminal response")
        return json.loads(response.read())


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("url", help="URL shown by the native MCP connection button")
    parser.add_argument("--changes", help='JSON process patch, e.g. {"wall_loops":4}; applied immediately by JusPrin')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    endpoint = urlsplit(args.url)
    if (endpoint.scheme != "http" or endpoint.hostname != "127.0.0.1" or
            not endpoint.port or endpoint.path != "/mcp" or endpoint.query or endpoint.fragment or endpoint.username):
        parser.error("Use the exact http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp local diagnostic URL")
    for method in ("server/discover", "tools/list"):
        print(json.dumps(call(endpoint, method), indent=2))
    workspace = call(endpoint, "tools/call", {"name": "workspace_inspect"})

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Pull requests

Before opening a pull request or posting on GitHub, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), including its "If you are an AI agent" section.

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
- For profile changes (`resources/profiles/<Vendor>/**`), check that `version` in the sibling `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` was bumped.
- For new or changed UI strings, check they follow [Writing translatable strings in the source](#writing-translatable-strings-in-the-source): no concatenated fragments, plural forms for counts, contexts for ambiguous words.
- For translation changes (`localization/i18n/**/*.po`), check that recurring terms match the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) for that language.

## Localization & translations

Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.

### Writing translatable strings in the source

Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:

- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.

See `.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/source-audit.md` for the full checklist.

### Terminology

- Use the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) as the source of truth for recurring terms, so the same English term is always rendered the same way within a language, and terms that must stay in English (brand/product names, acronyms, materials, file formats, G-code tokens, macros/variables/identifiers) are not translated.
- If a term's established translation changes, update both the affected `.po` files and the glossary (`developer_reference/glossary/<lang>.tsv` in the wiki, then regenerate) so they stay in sync.
- Translate the *meaning*, not the words. Check what the string actually controls before translating it — English reuses one word for different things. `Flow ratio` (multiplier), `Flow Rate` (throughput) and `Flow Dynamics` (pressure compensation) are three different terms; `extruder` may mean the toolhead, the feeder motor, or the nozzle depending on the string.
- Reuse one template per recurring message shape (`Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?`), even where the English wording varies.

---
name: reference-jusprin-windows-crash-repro
description: How to reproduce a JusPrin Windows crash on the jusprin-win-test VM without screen control — MCP driving, page heap, Sentry off, symbol lookup
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Recipe that reproduced JUSPRIN-APP-J (Windows divide crash) on 2026-11-26. VM notes and wrappers: `~/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/` (README.md, BUILDING.md, winssh.sh, winscp.sh, harness.ps1).

- Set gcloud to the ai-agent account first; VM is `jusprin-win-test`, project elegoo-backend, zone us-central1-a. Other sessions (release smoke tests) use it too: check transcripts for recent use and message them before taking it over.
- Run the installed app (`C:\Program Files\JusPrin`) from a scheduled task in session 1 (`Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1) with `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`, `--datadir` pointing at a robocopy of `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Roaming\JusPrin2` (signed in; skip projects/request-log/log/locks).
- Set `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN=none` so test crashes don't reach the real Sentry project (an unparsable DSN turns reporting off; see SentryClient.cpp).
- Drive it over MCP: the app writes `<datadir>\jusprin\mcp.json` with `url`; the bundled `C:\Program Files\JusPrin\python\python.exe` runs a small client (same protocol as tests/mcp/probe.py). Pass JSON args via files or Python scripts, not PowerShell-quoted strings.
- Out-of-bounds reads crash only sometimes in release builds; Windows full page heap makes them crash every time: IFEO key for `orca-slicer.exe`, `GlobalFlag=0x02000000`, `PageHeapFlags=0x3`. Remove it afterwards.
- Fault offset comes from the Application event log ("Application Error"); map it with the Breakpad .sym in Sentry (`/projects/sentry/jusprin-app/files/dsyms/`, match the DLL timestamp to the code id). FUNC records precede STACK CFI, so a partial download suffices.

content.text:
I've landed the record-file fix as one commit, `2a3023740b`, on jusprin-dev. It's in your local checkout only and not pushed. I reproduced the Windows divide crash (JUSPRIN-APP-J) on the VM and found its cause. The fix is written, but the Windows and macOS builds are still running, so I haven't confirmed it yet.

**Landing:** jusprin-dev had moved since I branched, but its files are identical to the commit I tested on. So the earlier test results still apply, and the only change since is one comment line.

**Sentry, and your question about remembering**
- **JUSPRIN-APP-K:** resolved in next release, with a note naming the commit. Sentry anchored it at 2.1.0, because the issue's last event came from 2.0.1 and 2.1.0 is now the newest release. That means an event from 2.1.0 would reopen it, even though 2.1.0 doesn't have the fix.
- **OBICO-MOBILE-24W, resolved earlier today:** its activity log shows the resolve went in as "next release" too, anchored at android 2.43+337, the live release. MOONRAKER-OBICO-TT is stored the same way and stayed quiet. If a different issue shows "resolved in the current release", tell me which one and I'll fix it.
- **Why I keep slipping:** the rule is already in my memory, but only as a reference note that I open when it seems relevant. I don't see it before every resolve.

**Decision needed:** should I add a hook to your Claude Code settings that blocks any request to sentry.obico.io that sets an issue to resolved without "next release" in it? This is the only reliable fix: the command is refused before it runs, whatever I remember. It costs one small script plus one settings entry. The alternative is a line in your global CLAUDE.md, which I always read but can still overlook. My pick is the hook, plus the CLAUDE.md line so the reason is written down. Should I add it?

**The Windows crash**
- **Reproduced:** I used the installed 2.1.0 on the VM with crash reporting turned off, so no test crashes reached Sentry. It needs three things:
  - a plate with several objects;
  - the last object holds a negative part;
  - an earlier object is cut with only one side kept, as the user's cuts did.
- **Every time:** with Windows' strict heap checking on, it crashed both times. It fails in the same function and on the same source line as the user's crash (`Selection.cpp:1166`). The same steps without the negative part pass.
- **Cause:** this is upstream OrcaSlicer code.
  1. After a cut, `apply_cut_object_to_model` is meant to tell the object list not to select the new piece until the 3D view is rebuilt.
  2. In PrusaSlicer, the argument that says so is `call_selection_changed`. In OrcaSlicer, that position is now `split_object`, so the `false` passed there stopped meaning anything.
  3. On Windows and Linux, the object list then selects the new piece straight away. The 3D view still holds the old objects' shapes under shifted positions, so the selection reads a negative part through the new piece's position in the list and reads past the end of its parts.
  4. macOS skips that selection code, which is why it never crashed there.
- **Fix:** 10 lines in `Plater.cpp`. They bring back the way to skip that selection, and the cut path uses it. It also stops a stray "objects were loaded as parts of cut object" notice after cuts with connectors, which matches PrusaSlicer. This also affects OrcaSlicer's own Cut tool, since it goes through the same function.

**Next:** run the crashing steps against the fixed Windows build and check that cuts still work on macOS. After that I'll turn off strict heap checking on the VM and clean up my test folders there.

Should I add the Sentry hook, or leave it for now?

**What triggers it:** the plate has several objects, the last one holds a negative part or a modifier, and the AI cuts an earlier object keeping only one side. The user's crash logs fit this: a Bambu Studio project with 27 objects, where every cut produced one piece.

**What I tested:**
- **Released 2.1.0 on the VM:** I turned on Windows' strict heap checking, which makes a read past the end of a list crash every time. With it on, the cut crashed both times I tried. It failed in the same function and on the same source line as the user's crashes (`Selection.cpp:1166`). The same steps without the negative part passed.
- **Fixed build on the VM:** the same steps passed twice, three cuts each run. After the cuts the app was healthy and the newest piece was selected.
- **Fixed build on macOS:** the same steps pass, the new piece ends up selected, and ordinary two-sided cuts still work.

**The fix:** 10 lines in `src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp`, which is OrcaSlicer's own code.
- After a cut, upstream means to hold off the object list's selection update until the 3D view is rebuilt. That stopped working when OrcaSlicer reused the argument for something else.
- The fix gives `load_model_objects` that argument back, and the cut passes `false`, as PrusaSlicer does.
- It also stops a stray "objects were loaded as parts of cut object" notice after a manual cut with connectors.
- OrcaSlicer's main branch has the same bug, so its own Cut tool can probably crash the same way on Windows and Linux. I haven't tested the Cut tool itself.

- **Sentry:** I added a note to JUSPRIN-APP-J with the cause and how to reproduce it. I'll resolve it in next release once the fix lands.

My earlier question about the Sentry hook is still open: should I add a hook that blocks any Sentry resolve that doesn't use "next release"?

Should I land the Windows crash fix as one commit on jusprin-dev, or hold it for now?

# Obico Gmail operations

Use these recipes after the authentication preflight in `SKILL.md`. Replace brace-delimited placeholders with resolved values. Quote all user-derived values and never interpolate an email body or other untrusted text into shell syntax.

Every command uses the fixed executable and mailbox:

```text
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog ... --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
```

## Read messages and threads

Search individual messages and include decoded bodies:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail messages search '{gmail_query}' --max {count} --include-body --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
```

Get one message by its resolved Gmail message ID:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail get '{message_id}' --format full --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
```

Read every message in a thread when history or forwarding headers matter:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail thread get '{thread_id}' --full --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
```

Download a resolved attachment to an explicit, narrow output path:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail attachment '{message_id}' '{attachment_id}' --out '{output_path}' --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
```

Resolve the attachment ID from the message first. Use a task-specific temporary directory or an exact requested path; do not let the CLI choose an implicit destination.

Search for a prior sent reply in a thread:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail messages search 'from:me in:sent thread:{thread_id}' --max 1 --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
```

If the result contains a sent message, treat a new send as a duplicate unless the calling workflow explicitly requires a follow-up.

## Drafts

List drafts, then inspect candidate drafts before matching by thread, recipient, and subject:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail drafts list --max 100 --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail drafts get '{draft_id}' --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
```

Create a reply draft with the prepared plain-text body supplied on standard input:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail drafts create --to '{recipient}' --subject 'Re: {original_subject}' --reply-to-message-id '{message_id}' --account k@obico.io --body-file - --json --no-input
```

Update the matching draft instead of creating a duplicate:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail drafts update '{draft_id}' --to '{recipient}' --subject 'Re: {original_subject}' --reply-to-message-id '{message_id}' --account k@obico.io --body-file - --json --no-input
```

For a new message rather than a reply, omit `--reply-to-message-id` and use the requested subject. After creating or updating, get the draft again and verify the recipient, subject, body, and thread relationship.

Send an already-reviewed draft only when the calling workflow authorizes sending that exact draft:

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail drafts send '{draft_id}' --account k@obico.io --json --no-input
```

Immediately before sending, get the draft again and ensure no internal notes, commands, UUIDs, infrastructure details, or operator-only text remain.


Send a new message by omitting `--reply-to-message-id` and using the requested subject. Perform the prior-sent search before replies, and verify the returned message and thread IDs after sending.

Archive a resolved thread by removing `INBOX`:


content.text:
# Update Config Skill

Modify Claude Code configuration by updating settings.json files.

## When Hooks Are Required (Not Memory)

If the user wants something to happen automatically in response to an EVENT, they need a **hook** configured in settings.json. Memory/preferences cannot trigger automated actions.

**These require hooks:**
- "Before compacting, ask me what to preserve" → PreCompact hook
- "After writing files, run prettier" → PostToolUse hook with Write|Edit matcher
- "When I run bash commands, log them" → PreToolUse hook with Bash matcher
- "Always run tests after code changes" → PostToolUse hook

**Hook events:** PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, Notification, SessionStart

## CRITICAL: Read Before Write

**Always read the existing settings file before making changes.** Merge new settings with existing ones - never replace the entire file.

## CRITICAL: Use AskUserQuestion for Ambiguity

When the user's request is ambiguous, use AskUserQuestion to clarify:
- Which settings file to modify (user/project/local)
- Whether to add to existing arrays or replace them
- Specific values when multiple options exist

## Decision: /config command vs Direct Edit

**Suggest the `/config` slash command** for these simple settings:
- `theme`, `editorMode`, `verbose`, `model`
- `language`, `alwaysThinkingEnabled`
- `permissions.defaultMode`

**Edit settings.json directly** for:
- Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.)
- Complex permission rules (allow/deny arrays)
- Environment variables
- MCP server configuration
- Plugin configuration

## Workflow

1. **Clarify intent** - Ask if the request is ambiguous
2. **Read existing file** - Use Read tool on the target settings file
3. **Merge carefully** - Preserve existing settings, especially arrays
4. **Edit file** - Use Edit tool (if file doesn't exist, ask user to create it first)
5. **Confirm** - Tell user what was changed

## Merging Arrays (Important!)

When adding to permission arrays or hook arrays, **merge with existing**, don't replace:

**WRONG** (replaces existing permissions):
```json
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(npm *)"] } }
```

**RIGHT** (preserves existing + adds new):
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git *)",      // existing
      "Edit(.claude)",    // existing
      "Bash(npm *)"       // new
    ]
  }
}
```

## Settings File Locations

Choose the appropriate file based on scope:

| File | Scope | Git | Use For |
|------|-------|-----|---------|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Global | N/A | Personal preferences for all projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Project | Commit | Team-wide hooks, permissions, plugins |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project | Gitignore | Personal overrides for this project |

Settings load in order: user → project → local (later overrides earlier).

## Settings Schema Reference

### Permissions
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(npm *)", "Edit(.claude)", "Read"],
    "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"],
    "ask": ["Edit(//etc/*)"],
    "defaultMode": "default" | "plan" | "acceptEdits" | "dontAsk",
    "additionalDirectories": ["/extra/dir"]
  }
}
```

**Permission Rule Syntax:**
- Exact match: `"Bash(npm run test)"`
- Prefix wildcard: `"Bash(git *)"` - matches `git`, `git status`, `git commit`, etc.
- Tool only: `"Read"` - allows all Read operations
- File paths: `"Edit(src/**)"` - path rules in `permissions` use `Edit(path)` for every file-writing tool (Write, Edit, NotebookEdit) and `Read(path)` for reads. `Write(path)`, `NotebookEdit(path)` and `Glob(path)` rules are not matched by file permission checks. Bare tool names (`"Write"`), deny/ask `Tool(param:value)` rules and hook `if` conditions still use each tool's own name

### Environment Variables
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DEBUG": "true",
    "MY_API_KEY": "value"
  }
}
```

### Model & Agent
```json
{
  "model": "sonnet",  // or "fable", "opus", "haiku", full model ID
  "agent": "agent-name",
  "alwaysThinkingEnabled": true
}
```

### Attribution (Commits & PRs)
```json
{
  "attribution": {
    "commit": "Custom commit trailer text",
    "pr": "Custom PR description text"
  }
}
```
Set `commit` or `pr` to empty string `""` to hide that attribution. To hide all of it, set both to `""` and also set `"sessionUrl": false`. Write this object form, not `"attribution": false`: older Claude Code versions reject true or false here and then skip the whole settings file.

### MCP Server Management
```json
{
  "enableAllProjectMcpServers": true,
  "enabledMcpjsonServers": ["server1", "server2"],
  "disabledMcpjsonServers": ["blocked-server"]
}
```

### Plugins
```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "formatter@anthropic-tools": true
  }
}
```
Plugin syntax: `plugin-name@source` where source is `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-plugins-official`, or `builtin`.

### Other Settings
- `language`: Preferred response language (e.g., "japanese")
- `cleanupPeriodDays`: Days to keep transcripts on this computer before automatic cleanup (default: 30; minimum 1)
- `respectGitignore`: Whether to respect .gitignore (default: true)
- `spinnerTipsEnabled`: Show tips in spinner
- `timeFormat`: Clock format for times shown in the UI: "auto" (default), "12-hour", "24-hour", "24-hour-utc", or a strftime pattern such as "%H:%M"
- `timeZone`: IANA time zone for times shown in the UI, e.g. "UTC" (default: system time zone)
- `spinnerVerbs`: Customize spinner verbs (`{ "mode": "append" | "replace", "verbs": [...] }`)
- `spinnerTipsOverride`: Override spinner tips (`{ "excludeDefault": true, "tips": ["Custom tip"] }`)
- `syntaxHighlightingDisabled`: Disable diff highlighting


## Hooks Configuration

Hooks run commands at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.

### Hook Structure
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "EVENT_NAME": [
      {
        "matcher": "ToolName|OtherTool",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "your-command-here",
            "timeout": 60,
            "statusMessage": "Running..."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Hook Events

| Event | Matcher | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| PermissionRequest | Tool name | Run before permission prompt |
| PreToolUse | Tool name | Run before tool, can block |
| PostToolUse | Tool name | Run after successful tool |
| PostToolUseFailure | Tool name | Run after tool fails |
| Notification | Notification type | Run on notifications |
| Stop | - | Run when Claude stops (including clear, resume, compact) |
| PreCompact | "manual"/"auto" | Before compaction |
| PostCompact | "manual"/"auto" | After compaction (receives summary) |
| UserPromptSubmit | - | When user submits |
| SessionStart | - | When session starts |

**Common tool matchers:** `Bash`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`

### Hook Types

**1. Command Hook** - Runs a shell command:
```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "prettier --write $FILE", "timeout": 30 }
```

**2. Prompt Hook** - Evaluates a condition with LLM:
```json
{ "type": "prompt", "prompt": "Is this safe? $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

**3. Agent Hook** - Runs an agent with tools:
```json
{ "type": "agent", "prompt": "Verify tests pass: $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

### Hook Input (stdin JSON)
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "tool_name": "Write",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt", "content": "..." },
  "tool_response": { "success": true }  // PostToolUse only
}
```

### Hook JSON Output

Hooks can return JSON to control behavior:

```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Warning shown to user in UI",
  "continue": false,
  "stopReason": "Message shown when blocking",
  "suppressOutput": false,
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Explanation for decision",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
    "additionalContext": "Context injected back to model"
  }
}
```

**Fields:**
- `systemMessage` - Display a message to the user (all hooks)
- `continue` - Set to `false` to block/stop (default: true)
- `stopReason` - Message shown when `continue` is false
- `suppressOutput` - Hide stdout from transcript (default: false)
- `decision` - "block" for PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks (deprecated for PreToolUse, use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision instead)
- `reason` - Explanation for decision
- `hookSpecificOutput` - Event-specific output (must include `hookEventName`):
  - `additionalContext` - Text injected into model context
  - `permissionDecision` - "allow", "deny", or "ask" (PreToolUse only)
  - `permissionDecisionReason` - Reason for the permission decision (PreToolUse only)
  - `updatedInput` - Modified tool input (PreToolUse only)

### Common Patterns

**Auto-format after writes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Log all bash commands:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.command' >> ~/.claude/bash-log.txt"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Stop hook that displays message to user:**

Command must output JSON with `systemMessage` field:
```bash
# Example command that outputs: {"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}
echo '{"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}'
```

**Run tests after code changes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath' | grep -E '\\.(ts|js)$' && npm test || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```


## Constructing a Hook (with verification)

Given an event, matcher, target file, and desired behavior, follow this flow. Each step catches a different failure class — a hook that silently does nothing is worse than no hook.

1. **Dedup check.** Read the target file. If a hook already exists on the same event+matcher, show the existing command and ask: keep it, replace it, or add alongside.

2. **Construct the command for THIS project — don't assume.** The hook receives JSON on stdin. Build a command that:
   - Extracts any needed payload safely — use `jq -r` into a quoted variable or `{ read -r f; ... "$f"; }`, NOT unquoted `| xargs` (splits on spaces)
   - Invokes the underlying tool the way this project runs it (npx/bunx/yarn/pnpm? Makefile target? globally-installed?)
   - Skips inputs the tool doesn't handle (formatters often have `--ignore-unknown`; if not, guard by extension)
   - Stays RAW for now — no `|| true`, no stderr suppression. You'll wrap it after the pipe-test passes.

3. **Pipe-test the raw command.** Synthesize the stdin payload the hook will receive and pipe it directly:
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Write|Edit`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<a real file from this repo>"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Bash`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart`: most commands don't read stdin, so `echo '{}' | <cmd>` suffices

   Check exit code AND side effect (file actually formatted, test actually ran). If it fails you get a real error — fix (wrong package manager? tool not installed? jq path wrong?) and retest. Once it works, wrap with `2>/dev/null || true` (unless the user wants a blocking check).

4. **Write the JSON.** Merge into the target file (schema shape in the "Hook Structure" section above). If this creates `.claude/settings.local.json` for the first time, add it to .gitignore — the Write tool doesn't auto-gitignore it.

5. **Validate syntax + schema in one shot:**

   `jq -e '.hooks.<event>[] | select(.matcher == "<matcher>") | .hooks[] | select(.type == "command") | .command' <target-file>`

   Exit 0 + prints your command = correct. Exit 4 = matcher doesn't match. Exit 5 = malformed JSON or wrong nesting. A broken settings.json silently disables ALL settings from that file — fix any pre-existing malformation too.

6. **Prove the hook fires** — only for `Pre|PostToolUse` on a matcher you can trigger in-turn (`Write|Edit` via Edit, `Bash` via Bash). `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart` fire outside this turn — skip to step 7.

   For a **formatter** on `PostToolUse`/`Write|Edit`: introduce a detectable violation via Edit (two consecutive blank lines, bad indentation, missing semicolon — something this formatter corrects; NOT trailing whitespace, Edit strips that before writing), re-read, confirm the hook **fixed** it. For **anything else**: temporarily prefix the command in settings.json with `echo "$(date) hook fired" >> /tmp/claude-hook-check.txt; `, trigger the matching tool (Edit for `Write|Edit`, a harmless `true` for `Bash`), read the sentinel file.

   **Always clean up** — revert the violation, strip the sentinel prefix — whether the proof passed or failed.

   **If proof fails but pipe-test passed and `jq -e` passed**: the settings watcher isn't watching `.claude/` — it only watches directories that had a settings file when this session started. The hook is written correctly. Tell the user to start a new session so the new settings load. You can't do this yourself.

7. **Handoff.** Tell the user the hook is live (or needs a new session per the watcher caveat), and that they can review, edit, or disable it later in the settings file you wrote. The UI only shows "Ran N hooks" if a hook errors or is slow — silent success is invisible by design.


## Example Workflows

### Adding a Hook

User: "Format my code after Claude writes it"

1. **Clarify**: Which formatter? (prettier, gofmt, etc.)
2. **Read**: `.claude/settings.json` (or create if missing)
3. **Merge**: Add to existing hooks, don't replace
4. **Result**:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Adding Permissions

User: "Allow npm commands without prompting"

1. **Read**: Existing permissions
2. **Merge**: Add `Bash(npm *)` to allow array
3. **Result**: Combined with existing allows

### Environment Variables

User: "Set DEBUG=true"

1. **Decide**: User settings (global) or project settings?
2. **Read**: Target file
3. **Merge**: Add to env object
```json
{ "env": { "DEBUG": "true" } }
```

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. **Replacing instead of merging** - Always preserve existing settings
2. **Wrong file** - Ask user if scope is unclear
3. **Invalid JSON** - Validate syntax after changes
4. **Forgetting to read first** - Always read before write

## Troubleshooting Hooks

If a hook isn't running:
1. **Check the settings file** - Read ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json
2. **Verify JSON syntax** - Invalid JSON silently fails
3. **Check the matcher** - Does it match the tool name? (e.g., "Bash", "Write", "Edit")
4. **Check hook type** - Is it "command", "prompt", or "agent"?
5. **Test the command** - Run the hook command manually to see if it works
6. **Use --debug** - Run `claude --debug` to see hook execution logs


## Full Settings JSON Schema

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "$schema": {
      "description": "JSON Schema reference for Claude Code settings",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "apiKeyHelper": {
      "description": "Path to a script that outputs authentication values",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "proxyAuthHelper": {
      "description": "Shell command that outputs a Proxy-Authorization header value (EAP)",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "awsCredentialExport": {
      "description": "Path to a script that exports AWS credentials",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "awsAuthRefresh": {
      "description": "Path to a script that refreshes AWS authentication",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "gcpAuthRefresh": {
      "description": "Command to refresh GCP authentication (e.g., gcloud auth application-default login)",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "processWrapper": {
      "description": "Corporate launcher argv prefix for the background-agent supervisor, the sessions and workers it hosts, and the other covered background processes listed in the Claude Code corporate-launcher documentation. Equivalent to the CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER environment variable, which takes precedence when set. Honored from managed settings, a --settings/SDK-supplied settings file, and user settings, in that precedence order; project and local settings are ignored.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "policyHelper": {
      "description": "Executable that computes managed settings at startup. Honored only from admin-controlled policy sources.",
      "type": "object",

Nothing runs them unless the model asks. Also refuses file-tool writes to Claude Code settings files, inside the working directories too, and takes EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree, which move the working directory, out of the tools on offer (a setting of the program that starts Claude Code can keep them). Does not limit shell commands, MCP tools, the programs that hooks run, or the memory tools.         "blockReadsExemptPaths": {
          "description": "For the program that starts Claude Code: read only from --settings and from settings that program sends while the session runs; ignored in user, project, local and managed settings. The paths do not become working directories, so blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories refuses writes to them, and they are not told to MCP servers or to the model. Each path counts as written: a link in it is not followed and a pattern is not expanded, so list every spelling that a read may arrive by. Ignored: an entry that starts with ~, has a \"..\" segment or has white space at either end (as written or once normalized), a relative or network path, and the root of a filesystem.             "default": "",
            "type": "string"

To decide what lies inside a listed working directory, Claude Code takes it as written and follows no link at it, so a link that later stands in its place gives the file tools no access to where the link leads. List real paths: the files of a listed path that runs through a link count as outside the working directories, because where they really are lies outside it. List a mapped network drive by its drive-letter path: Claude Code still derives the UNC form of that path by itself and adds it, as for any mapped drive. A file path that is itself spelled as a UNC path is judged as written, so a link on the share is not seen by that spelling. It adds no working directory and allows nothing. Once listed, a path stays so until the process ends, also if later settings leave it out. Ignored: an entry that is not already normalized (a relative path, one that starts with ~, a \"..\" segment, a separator at its end unless it is a filesystem root, forward slashes on Windows, white space at either end). Does not change what sandboxed commands may write.",

          "items": {
            "default": "",
            "type": "string"
          }

A path is refused if it, or where its links lead, lies in a listed path, in any letter case, or above one that no Read deny rule covers (a Grep or Glob rooted there would walk into it; a deny rule keeps those two out, unless a \"!\" rule is also in force); for a search the path judged is its root, not each file found below it. Still let through: a working directory, or for reads a path of blockReadsExemptPaths, that is the listed path or lies inside it, and the files that Claude Code keeps for the session. It allows nothing, binds what those three settings bind, and does nothing with all of them off. Each path counts as written: a link in it is not followed, so list every spelling. Once listed, a path stays listed for the life of the process. Ignored: a relative path, and one that starts with ~, has a \"..\" segment or has white space at either end.           "items": {
            "default": "",
            "type": "string"
          }
```

The hook is in. When any agent tries to resolve a Sentry issue without "next release", Claude Code now stops and asks you to confirm instead of refusing outright. It covers every project, because it lives in your user settings.

**What it catches:**
- A plain resolve, and "resolved in release X".
- Requests sent with `curl` or Python, including a request body read from a file.

**What it lets through without asking:**
- Resolves that use next release.
- Ignores and other status changes.
- Read-only Sentry calls, and searches like `grep` that only mention those words.

I checked all of these against sample commands.

**Tested:**
- **Pipe test:** I fed the script 12 sample commands, and each one was asked about or let through as expected.
- **Fresh session:** I ran a headless Claude session with the new settings, in bypass mode like yours, and told it to run a harmless `echo` shaped like a plain resolve. The hook caught it, and the command did not run. In a normal session you would see a prompt with this text:

  > This command resolves a Sentry issue without "next release"… Allow it only if a plain resolve is really what you want, such as a one-off test issue.

**Not tested:**
- **This session:** it loaded its settings before I added the hook, so the hook only applies to sessions started from now on, or to this one after a restart.
- **The interactive prompt:** I haven't seen it appear in a normal session with someone there to answer. The headless test only shows that the hook fires and is obeyed.

**One side effect:** the sentry-triage skill resolves some issues on purpose with a plain resolve, such as test-probe issues once they go quiet. Those resolves will now ask you too. If a scheduled triage run has nobody watching, that resolve won't happen, and the issue stays open until a later run or until you resolve it yourself.

**Files:**
- The check itself is `~/.claude/hooks/sentry-resolve-guard.py`.
- The hook entry is under `hooks.PreToolUse` in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Nothing else in that file changed.

--- 2026-11-26T17:03:33.439Z 
 You were right to question it. The crash is real, but the explanation I gave was wrong, and the fix I proposed only covers the symptom.

**What's actually happening**

The phrase "several webcams and none marked primary" came from the commit message of the November 24 fix. I repeated it without checking it. It isn't what the data shows:

- **The agents always mark one webcam primary.** Both the OctoPrint and Klipper agents mark exactly one webcam as primary whenever they report any webcams.
- **The affected printers have no webcam right now.** I read both affected printers' webcam settings from production. Both run moonraker-obico 2.0.9. One reports an **empty** webcam list. The other reports one primary webcam, which shouldn't crash today.
- **An empty list is a normal state.** The Klipper agent sends an empty list when every webcam has streaming turned off, or when starting the stream fails (`moonraker_obico/webcam_stream.py`). So "this printer has no webcam right now" is legitimate, not an upstream bug.
- **The crash needs one more step.** The person must have rotated this printer's webcam once while it still had a camera. The app saved that rotation, and every later screen tries to look it up by the name of a primary webcam that no longer exists.

For the second user, I'd guess the stream failed at that moment, so the list was briefly empty. That's a hypothesis, not something I've verified.

**Why the earlier fix was weak**

The app has the same "find the primary webcam, then read its rotation" code pasted into four screens:
- `PrinterItem.js` (printer list row)
- `PrinterCard.js` (printer list card)
- `PrinterControls.js` (printer screen)
- `FullScreenWebCam.js`

The earlier fix added a null check to one of the four. Users with this state stopped crashing on the list and started crashing on the next screen. Adding `?.` to two more copies would be the same patch again.

**What I propose instead**

Replace the four copies with one shared hook. It returns no webcam and no rotation when the printer has no webcam, and every screen uses it. Before changing anything, I'd extend the existing Jest test to render the printer screen with an empty webcam list and a saved rotation. That reproduces this crash. Then I'd make the change and show the test passing.

I posted a correction note on OBICO-MOBILE-24W in Sentry so the wrong explanation doesn't stand.

Should I make the shared-hook fix in TSDApp now, or leave it for later?
--- 2026-11-26T17:10:44.899Z

**What changed**
- **New shared function**, `src/hooks/usePrimaryWebcam.js`. It returns the printer's default webcam, which is its only webcam or the one marked primary. It also returns the rotation the person saved for that webcam. When the printer reports no webcam, it returns no webcam and a rotation of 0. The comment in the file explains that this is a normal state.
- **All four screens now use it:** the printer list row (`PrinterItem.js`), the printer list card (`PrinterCard.js`), the printer controls screen (`PrinterControls.js`) and the full-screen webcam view (`FullScreenWebCam.js`). Their four pasted copies of the lookup are gone.

**How I tested it**
- **Reproduced the crash first.** I wrote a Jest test that renders the real printer controls screen with the state I found in production: an empty webcam list and a saved rotation. Before the change it failed with the same error as the Android crash in Sentry, `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` at `PrinterControls.js:34`. After the change it passes.
- **Added unit tests for the shared function.** They cover one webcam, several webcams with one primary, an empty list, a missing list, an unknown printer, and a saved rotation with no webcam.
- **Results:** all 10 Jest tests pass. ESLint reports no errors on the changed files. Its 5 warnings are on lines this change didn't touch.
- **Not tested in the running app.** Doing that needs an Android build connected to a Klipper printer whose webcam stream is off or failing, plus a rotation saved earlier. The Jest test renders the real screen with the real store lookup, but it isn't the same as trying it on a device.

**obico-server web frontend**
It doesn't have this bug. Every place that reads a webcam field either checks first that the webcam exists or loops over the webcams the printer actually reported. That covers the printer card, the shared printer page and the printer control page. The saved rotation is keyed by printer and stream id, and it falls back to `0` when there is no webcam. Sentry agrees: the web frontend project has no errors from a missing webcam in the last 90 days.
--- 2026-11-26T17:14:49.647Z 
 The mobile webcam fix is landed on TSDApp master as one commit, `d8ab34b7`, and pushed. In Sentry, OBICO-MOBILE-24W is resolved for the next release, anchored to Android 2.43+337, the release that's out now. If a later build crashes this way again, Sentry reopens it as a regression. Its email is in Trash. Jest ran 16 of 16 tests passing. The one test file that failed to load, `__tests__/App-test.js`, also fails on the commit before mine, so it was already broken.

I moved on to the next issues: the JusPrin crash after dividing an object, and the save failure that followed it. I've diagnosed both from the code, but I haven't reproduced either, so per your rule I haven't fixed them. I posted the findings on both Sentry issues.

**The divide crash (JUSPRIN-APP-J) is Windows and Linux only.**
- Splitting an object deletes the original from the model and adds the pieces.
- On Windows and Linux, adding each piece to the object list immediately selects it in the 3D view. That happens before the 3D scene is rebuilt, so the selection reads a model object by an index that has just gone stale, and that read hits garbage memory.
- The macOS build skips that selection step (it sits in `#ifndef __WXOSX__` in `GUI_ObjectList.cpp`), so it can't crash on a Mac. Reproducing it needs a Windows build on the `jusprin-win-test` VM.
- One thing I can't explain yet: why the Cut tool in the normal interface, which uses the same function, doesn't crash the same way.

**The save failure (JUSPRIN-APP-K) is probably caused by those crashes.**
- Every assistant action gets a number such as `t-12`. The counter lives in the project state file, which is saved later. The record of each action is written to disk at once.
- If the app dies between those two writes, the next run hands out `t-12` again. Writing that record fails with "operation version record already exists", and the person is told the project wasn't saved.
- This user had just crashed three times, which fits. This hypothesis can be tested on this Mac: run an assistant action, kill the app, restart it, and run another.

**Decision needed: which of the two to reproduce first.**
- **Save failure first, on this Mac (my pick).** It costs nothing extra, it's quick, and it protects everyone, because any crash or forced quit sets up the same failure.
- **The divide crash.** It needs a JusPrin build on the shared Windows VM, which takes a long time and slows down the other sessions building there. Then I'd have to drive a divide through the assistant on the VM.

- **Save failure (JUSPRIN-APP-K):** that session's latest commit on jusprin-dev, `e895b0d065` from today, changes who is told when a save fails. If the operating system refuses the save, for example a full disk or a read-only folder, the person sees the system's reason and nothing is reported to us. Any other save failure is reported to us. def syndicate_mismatch(get_response):
    """Reports a request whose host, X-Obico-Syndicate header (or the cookie
    syndicate_header leaves) and signed-in account name different syndicates:
    to Sentry, and as one log line. A header naming only a brand, such as
    Yumi's, is no mismatch; brands are not compared.

    With settings.SYNDICATE_MISMATCH 'refuse', an account of another syndicate
    than the host's is refused before the view runs. That refuses an Obico admin
    impersonating a Kingroon account on Obico's host too; they would use
    Kingroon's host. An account an API view signs in by token is known only
    after the view, so it is reported, not refused."""
    def middleware(request):
        if (settings.SYNDICATE_MISMATCH == 'refuse' and request.user.is_authenticated
                and request.user.syndicate_id != host_syndicate(request).id):
            _report_syndicate_mismatch(request)
            raise PermissionDenied("An account of another syndicate than the host's")
        response = get_response(request)
        _report_syndicate_mismatch(request)
        return response

    return middleware


def _report_syndicate_mismatch(request):
    signed_in = request.user.is_authenticated
    header = header_syndicate_name(request)
    if not signed_in and header is None:
        return
    host = host_syndicate(request)
    account_differs = signed_in and request.user.syndicate_id != host.id
    header_differs = header is not None and header != host.name and header in settings.SYNDICATES
    if not (account_differs or header_differs):
        return
    details = {
        'host': request.get_host(),
        'host_syndicate': host.name,
        'header_syndicate': header,
        'account_syndicate': request.user.syndicate.name if signed_in else None,
        'path': request.path,
        'user_agent': request.META.get('HTTP_USER_AGENT', ''),
    }
    LOGGER.warning('syndicate_mismatch %s', json.dumps(details))
    sentry_sdk.capture_message('Syndicate mismatch', level='warning',
                               tags={key: details[key] for key in ('host_syndicate', 'header_syndicate', 'account_syndicate')},
                               contexts={'syndicate_mismatch': details})

"""Which syndicate and which brand a request gets.

A syndicate is a set of accounts (app.models.Syndicate), picked by the request's
host (SiteSyndicate). A brand is only how pages and emails look (settings.BRANDS):
picked per request, never stored, never used to pick accounts.

Until settings.SYNDICATE_MISMATCH is 'refuse', the syndicate follows the order the
server always had: the signed-in account's, then the X-Obico-Syndicate header's,
then the host's. app.middleware.syndicate_mismatch reports every request where
they disagree, so the switch to the host alone is made on evidence."""
import re

from django.conf import settings

from app.models.syndicate_models import Syndicate, SiteSyndicate
from config.settings import SITE_USES_HTTPS

BASE = 'base'
JUSPRIN_V1_BRAND = 'jusprin'
# JusPrin v1's built-in browser. JusPrin 2 names OrcaSlicer's release after its
# own (jusprin/v2/app_version.py), and its pages open in a browser of its own.
JUSPRIN_V1_USER_AGENT = re.compile(r'^JusPrin(?!.*\sOrcaSlicer/)')


def host_syndicate(request):
    # request.site is TopDomainMatchingCurrentSiteMiddleware's: an unknown host
    # gets the first site.
    return SiteSyndicate.objects.select_related('syndicate').get(site_id=request.site.id).syndicate


def header_syndicate_name(request):
    """The name a mobile app's X-Obico-Syndicate header gives, carried over by
    app.middleware.syndicate_header's cookie. A brand's name, and in the old
    order also a syndicate's."""
    return request.META.get('HTTP_X_OBICO_SYNDICATE') or None


def syndicate_from_request(request):
    if settings.SYNDICATE_MISMATCH == 'log':
        if request.user.is_authenticated:
            return request.user.syndicate
        name = header_syndicate_name(request)
        syndicate = Syndicate.objects.filter(name=name).first() if name else None
        if syndicate:
            return syndicate
    return host_syndicate(request)


def brand_from_request(request):
    """Kingroon's and JusPrin 2's hosts show their own brand. On Obico's hosts,
    JusPrin v1 shows its brand, a mobile app the brand its header names, and
    anything else the request's syndicate's brand."""
    host = host_syndicate(request)
    if host.name != BASE:
        return brand_of_syndicate(host.name)
    if JUSPRIN_V1_USER_AGENT.match(request.META.get('HTTP_USER_AGENT', '')):
        return JUSPRIN_V1_BRAND
    header = header_syndicate_name(request)
    if header in settings.BRANDS:
        return header
    return brand_of_syndicate(syndicate_from_request(request).name)


def brand_of_syndicate(syndicate_name):
    return settings.SYNDICATES[syndicate_name]['brand']


def brand_settings(brand):
    return settings.BRANDS[brand]


SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE = {}

def build_full_url_for_syndicate(url, syndicate_name):
    global SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE
    if syndicate_name not in SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE:
        # The syndicate's first site by domain, as Site's ordering made it when
        # sites were a many-to-many.
        SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name] = SiteSyndicate.objects.filter(
            syndicate__name=syndicate_name).order_by('site__domain').first().site.domain

    domain_name = SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name]

    protocol = 'https://' if SITE_USES_HTTPS else 'http://'
    normalized_url = re.sub(r'^/', '', url)
    return '{}{}/{}'.format(protocol, domain_name, normalized_url)

    term, then deletes the account, and with it its credits, tokens and kept
    chats (jusprin.apps). A JusPrin 2 account is a user of its own, apart from

"""Signing in to JusPrin from inside the desktop app, by email.

The app talks to allauth's own API for apps (allauth.headless, the "app"
client): it asks for a code and confirms it, or logs in with a password. Only
those views are mounted (urls.py), not the whole API, so nothing else that
allauth.headless serves, such as its sign-up without the website's reCAPTCHA,
becomes reachable. Between steps the app carries allauth's session token. A
finished sign-in ends in what the browser sign-in ends in: an OAuth2 access and
refresh token for the JusPrin 2 application (TokenStrategy).

Two things allauth does not do here. It looks an address up across every
syndicate, so the code request looks it up in the request's syndicate as the
website does (users_by_email). And it sends no code to an
address without an account, so the code request makes that account first, with
no usable password, as the website's sign-up would; confirming the code marks
the address verified.
"""
from allauth.account import signals
from allauth.account.adapter import get_adapter
from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from allauth.account.utils import setup_user_email
from allauth.core import context, ratelimit
from allauth.headless.account import views as headless
from allauth.headless.account.inputs import LoginInput, RequestLoginCodeInput
from allauth.headless.constants import Client
from allauth.headless.tokens.strategies.sessions import SessionTokenStrategy
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import transaction
from oauth2_provider.models import Application
from oauth2_provider.settings import oauth2_settings
from oauthlib.common import Request as OAuthRequest

from app.accounts import users_by_email
from app.models import User
from lib.syndicate import syndicate_from_request

SCOPE = 'read write'


class TokenStrategy(SessionTokenStrategy):
        return token


class SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput(RequestLoginCodeInput):
    def clean_email(self):
        # RequestLoginCodeForm.clean_email, with the account looked up in the
        # request's syndicate and an inactive one refused rather than
        # passed over, so no second account is made beside it.
        email = self.cleaned_data['email']
        if not email:
            return email
        request = context.request
        if not ratelimit.consume(request, action='request_login_code', key=email.lower()):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('too_many_login_attempts')
        users = users_by_email(email, syndicate_from_request(request))
        if users and not any(user.is_active for user in users):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('account_inactive')
        active = [user for user in users if user.is_active]
        self._user = active[0] if active else None
        return email


class ActiveAccountLoginInput(LoginInput):
    def clean(self):
        # The right password for an inactive account is refused as the code
        # request refuses it, rather than as a sign-in left unfinished.
        cleaned_data = super().clean()
        login = getattr(self, 'login', None)
        if login is not None and not login.user.is_active:
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('account_inactive')
        return cleaned_data


class LoginView(headless.LoginView):
    input_class = ActiveAccountLoginInput


class RequestLoginCodeView(headless.RequestLoginCodeView):
    input_class = SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput

    def post(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        if self.input._user is None:
            self.input._user = _new_account(request, self.input.cleaned_data['email'])
        return super().post(request, *args, **kwargs)


def _new_account(request, email: str):
    """Makes the account for an address that has none, as the website's sign-up
    does (the account adapter, then the address as an unverified primary
    EmailAddress), with no usable password. Confirming the code verifies the
    address."""
    adapter = get_adapter(request)
    with transaction.atomic():
        user = adapter.new_user(request)
        user.email = email
        user.syndicate = syndicate_from_request(request)
        adapter.populate_username(request, user)
        user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        setup_user_email(request, user, [EmailAddress(email=email)])
    signals.user_signed_up.send(sender=User, request=request, user=user)
    return user

No real customer can hit the "Syndicate mismatch" warning (OBICO-SERVER-B2B). Your own JusPrin 2 app caused every new event, because it is signed in with your Obico account rather than a JusPrin 2 account. I resolved the issue in Sentry, posted a note explaining why, and moved its two alert emails to Trash.

**What happens:**
1. You click "Credits and plans" in JusPrin 2.
2. The app asks the server for a one-time link, and the link signs the browser in as whichever account the app is signed in with. For you, that's your Obico account.
3. Since November 23, production refuses an Obico account on `jusprinv2.obico.io`. So every page, including the JusPrin 1 move page, returns an error and gets logged to Sentry.

**Why it can't happen to customers:** I queried production. The JusPrin 2 app has 171 active sign-ins. 170 belong to JusPrin 2 accounts, and one belongs to your Obico account. That one dates from November 3, before production started refusing Obico accounts there. Since then, every way of signing in to JusPrin 2 picks a JusPrin 2 account, so another Obico-account sign-in can't be created.

**For you:** your app keeps failing on those pages until you sign out of JusPrin 2 and back in. After that it uses a JusPrin 2 account, which keeps its own plan and credits apart from your Obico account.

I resolved the issue without "next release", because nothing was fixed. Any new event reopens it, and an event from anyone but you would be a real mismatch.

My earlier explanation was wrong in two places. Your Obico account isn't mixed up, and your normal JusPrin 2 app probably isn't the one causing this.

**The date I gave:** I tied the old sign-in to November 23, when production started refusing Obico accounts on the JusPrin 2 site. The date that actually matters is November 5. Before then, JusPrin 2 had no accounts of its own, and every JusPrin 2 sign-in used an Obico account.

- **November 5:** commit `1845fe74b9` in tsd-enterprise gave JusPrin 2 its own accounts, separate from Obico's.
- **November 10:** you signed in again and got a separate JusPrin 2 account under the same email. Your sign-ins on November 11 and 13 also went to that account.

So production now has three accounts under your email:

| Account | Created |
|---|---|
| Obico | 2019 |
| Kingroon | 2024 |
| JusPrin 2 | November 10 |

**What caused the events:** some JusPrin 2 install still holds the November 3 sign-in. On November 26 at 00:21 UTC it opened "Credits and plans" from your home IP. That signed the browser in as your Obico account on the JusPrin 2 site, and the site refused those pages. I can't tell which install it was, because these sign-ins last 100 years and record no last use. My guess is an older dev build or app data folder on one of your machines that hasn't signed in since November 3.

**Correction:** I said earlier that your app would keep failing until you signed out. That only applies to whichever install still holds the November 3 sign-in. If you find it, sign out and back in, or delete its app data. Your current app is most likely already on the JusPrin 2 account.

content.text:
The old sign-in is now revoked on the server, so this can't happen again from that install. I couldn't find the install itself, because it isn't on this Mac.

**How I searched:** I found 114 JusPrin 2 settings files on this Mac. These are the files where the app stores its sign-in: your installed app, the staging copy, and many test copies that Claude sessions made. I compared a short fingerprint of each stored sign-in against the server's copies, so no token was printed. None of them held the November 3 sign-in.
- Your installed JusPrin 2 is signed in to your JusPrin 2 account, the one created November 10.
- The others are your staging copy and test sign-ins.

I also checked whether a Claude session on this Mac opened those pages on November 26 at 00:21 UTC. None did. The visits came from your home IP, so my guess is another computer at home, such as a PC or laptop with an older JusPrin 2 build that hasn't signed in since November 3.

**What I did:** I signed out that old sign-in from the server side, in production. That works wherever the install is. Whichever install held it will show as signed out the next time it checks, and signing in again there will give it your JusPrin 2 account. Afterwards I checked that your Obico account has no JusPrin 2 sign-ins left, and that your JusPrin 2 account's three sign-ins weren't touched.

I added a note about this to OBICO-SERVER-B2B in Sentry.
